question: The Italian Government’s Decree-Law No 34/2023 (converted into Law No 56/2023) established, in Article 24, a fund for asbestos victims that should intervene in favour of workers in publicly owned companies who have contracted asbestos-related diseases while working at shipyards – or in favour of their heirs.

The fund can also be accessed by investee companies that have to pay compensation for material and non-material damage to workers, as explained in the Decree-Law and the Interministerial Implementing Decree of 16 July 2024. The legislation therefore provides that only publicly owned companies active in the shipbuilding sector (i.e.
Fincantieri, the only applicant in 2023) may use this fund to cover the costs of compensation for workers who are victims of asbestos, thereby giving them an advantage over competitors in the sector.

Given that the objective of the fund could be effectively achieved by allocating the entire amount directly to the workers affected (or the heirs), can the Commission clarify whether only allowing publicly owned companies active in the shipbuilding sector access to the fund might in fact constitute unwarranted State aid capable of distorting competition within the meaning of Article 107 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (17.1.

2025) With regards to the question of the Honourable Members concerning the conformity with the internal market and the rules on competition (Article 107 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union) of the Fund established by Decree-Law 34/2023 (converted into Law 56/2023) in favour of workers of publicly owned companies, who have contracted asbestosrelated diseases during their employment at shipyards, the Commission is in contact with the Italian authorities to further clarify the facts of the case and can therefore not comment any further at this stage.

The Commission also recalls that, in general, it is for the Member State to assess if a specific measure involves State aid within the meaning of EU State aid rules. If a measure constitutes State aid, the Member State needs to notify the measure to the Commission before putting it into effect. Furthermore, national courts have an important role in enforcing EU law, including in State aid law.
